prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a chosen protein to a ubiquitin ligase for destruction, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target through which molecular glues act.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B020 as the whole prize, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After the full first-round exchange, six of eight members include degradation and five make it the whole prize, and nobody has disputed its scientific validity or reproduction. The citation should rest on the chemical principle, which answers the chair's question about a Medicine claim. A small molecule induces a ligase-target ternary complex, and the outcome depends on proximity, cooperativity and ubiquitin transfer, not on occupancy. That is a physical-organic and structural description of a molecular recognition event, and the chemistry (linker design, ternary-complex cooperativity, the structural basis of cereblon recruitment) is where the achievement lies. The cereblon strand supplies the mechanism for thalidomide-type drugs that are already in patients, so the claim that this is a prize for a clinically unproven idea is weaker than it first sounds. I regard the third seat as a choice between two defensible contributions, and I explain below why I still prefer Handa. I did not move my own first-round choice back to nitrogenase, since the response from colleagues has been consistent that attribution and lack of committee support make it a candidate for a later year.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, and a prize now is a judgment that the principle will stand even if early clinical programmes disappoint. The three-person limit leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and Sakamoto and Kim are the first authors of the 2001 paper that founded the PROTAC concept, so the omission is uncomfortable and should be acknowledged openly. The PROTAC and glue strands have separate histories, and a single citation can look like a compromise. There remains a fair view, held by Aqvist and Chabes, that a mature candidate such as B061 or B063 is more overdue than a modality still maturing.

responses.point: Aqvist asked me directly whether the unresolved substrate-reduction mechanism in nitrogenase affects maturity, and he prefers Ciulli to Handa as the third name and a citation limited to bifunctional degraders.
responses.response: On nitrogenase, yes, it matters. The structures of the cofactor are stable and independently confirmed, but how N2 binds and is reduced on the FeMo-cofactor is still debated, so the central chemical question is not settled. That is a maturity problem on top of the five-name attribution problem, and it is the main reason I am not pressing B028 against B020. On the third seat I take Ciulli's contribution seriously: structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned an idea into a design discipline. But that work builds on the 2001 concept, while the identification of cereblon was an independent discovery that explained an entire drug class. A citation limited to bifunctional degraders also leaves the clinically established glue drugs without an explanation. I would therefore keep Handa, while accepting that a configuration with Ciulli is defensible and that I could vote for it if it is what unites the B020 supporters.

responses.point: Chabes proposes two parts, base editing (Liu alone) and degradation (Crews and Deshaies only), and wants nitrogenase kept for a later year.
responses.response: I agree on nitrogenase. On the two-part prize, I do not think it improves on B020 alone. His own case against shows why: base editing follows the 2020 prize closely and clinical data are still young, and a degradation part reduced to Crews and Deshaies drops the cereblon mechanism that makes the molecular-glue half chemically understood. Pairing a young modality with another young modality seems to me to compound the timing risk and not to spread it. Where we agree is that Liu alone is the defensible attribution for B047, and I would support that as a standalone choice if B020 failed on attribution. I would not use the three-person budget on a second part when the single part already has an open question about its third name.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the PROTAC and glue strands can be worded as one principle without implying that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are not contributors, and whether the Medicine overlap should shape the citation.
responses.response: I think one citation works if it names the shared mechanism, the recruitment of a ubiquitin ligase to a chosen protein by a small molecule, and credits the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism as the two foundations of that mechanism. The text I propose speaks of the principle and of what the named laureates did, and does not claim that no one else contributed. On timing I stand by what I said in round 1: the glue drugs are established medicines and the cereblon mechanism is confirmed structurally, so what is early is PROTAC clinical outcome, not the principle. I would not make the prize wait for a first PROTAC approval. On Medicine, I would emphasise ternary-complex recognition and event-driven catalysis in the citation, as this is where a chemistry committee has the strongest claim.

responses.point: Somfai continues to prefer C-N coupling (B044) as the mature, cleanly attributed choice, and he treats B020's lack of an approved drug and its eight credited names as a difficulty.
responses.response: I accept that B044 has the cleaner attribution and a mature mechanistic base, and I would not dispute its science. My difficulty is the one he states himself, namely that it reads as a second prize for the cross-coupling idea recognised in 2010, together with the Kosugi priority question, and only two members rank it. His round-1 view that B020 has the stronger claim if the committee wants a new conceptual direction is, I think, the right way to frame the choice. On B020 attribution, the eight credited names are a reason to state the citation narrowly, around the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism, and to say openly that the three-person limit is why others are not named.

responses.point: Aili moved from Ciulli to Handa for the third seat, on the argument that the cereblon discovery is what makes the glue half mechanistically coherent.
responses.response: I welcome the move and I agree with the reasoning. It also means that four of the six members who include B020 now name Handa, and that the remaining difference is mostly about Ciulli. I would add that this is a judgment about independent discovery and not about merit, and that the committee should state it that way in the record, since Ciulli's design work is real.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers Handa or Ciulli for the third seat, and whether Aqvist and Chabes can accept Handa or would require the citation to be limited to bifunctional degraders.
Whether a prize for B020 will be seen as premature before any PROTAC approval, and whether one more year would change the picture materially.
Whether the omission of Sakamoto and Kim, who were first authors of the 2001 PROTAC paper, would be criticised outside the committee.
I am relying on memory for priority dates of the 2001 PROTAC paper and the 2010 cereblon work and have not checked them.
Whether the Medicine committee would regard B020 as its own territory, which I cannot assess from the information available.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to any proposed laureate in my preferred configuration. My research field (respiratory proton transfer) is close to B028, which is now only an alternative, and I disclose that as a possible bias in how I weigh it. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose preferred part is B007 and not mine. I do not request recusal.
